title: Theme engine
subject: ui
summary: How the engine compiles a theme: the selector model, specificity, the composition variables, output principles and structure, smart bleed, the build pipeline, what the engine does not do.

axioms.text: The engine emits only what the theme declares; a zero theme is zero cascade lines.
Cascade priority is CSS source order and specificity, never a variable chain.
The engine's only structural knowledge is the conventions file; everything else it reads from the theme and the elements table.

purpose.intro: The engine turns a theme declaration into the one CSS file an application loads. This document is for whoever changes the engine; a theme author reads the Theme document and never needs this one.

reference.statement: Two attributes, never on the same node:

snippets.code:
<div element="surface--card">        element = {family}--{element}
<div layout="left-sidebar">          layout = bare name (no prefix)
snippets.caption: html

claims.text: Rules: only emit CSS for `part` values **explicitly declared** in the theme under that surface's `parts` field. An undeclared `part` is inert — zero CSS emitted. This prevents developers from using `part` as a free styling escape hatch. `part` is never used on the same node as `element` or `layout`.
Selector emitted: `[element="surface--card"] [part="body"] { ... }`

reference.statement: `part="name"` marks a structural sub-region of a themed ancestor. Use it on plain divs that a designer needs to control (padding, gap, background) without giving the div a full element identity.

snippets.code:
<div element="surface--card">
  <div part="body">      ← designer controls interior here
  <div part="actions">   ← designer controls gap here
snippets.caption: html

reference.topic: Selector Model › Axis attributes (bare, no data- prefix)

reference.statement: CSS source order + specificity handles cascade priority. No variable chains or bridge systems. The engine emits rules in this order:

snippets.code:
[element^="surface--"]                                  L2 family (lowest)
[element="surface--card"]                               L3 element
[element="surface--card"][emphasis="primary"]            axis (emphasis first)
[element="surface--card"][status="error"]                axis (status later = wins)
[element="surface--card"]:hover                         pseudo-class (highest)
[element="surface--card"][emphasis="primary"]:hover      compound (most specific)
[concept="X"] [element="surface--card"]                 concept (2 selectors)
[element="A"] [element="B"]                             contextual (2 selectors)

claims.text: Everything else is plain CSS. Padding, radius, shadow, cursor, transition, typography — set directly, no variables.

reference.statement: 5 CSS custom properties handle cross-property composition:

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Variable | Why it exists |
|----------|---------------|
| `--bg` | Tint mixes into background via `color-mix()` |
| `--fg` | `smart-bw` computes foreground from background |
| `--tint` | One color modifies both background and border |
| `--border-color` | Tint mixes into border via `color-mix()` |
| `--bg-alpha` | Alpha composites with transparent |

claims.text: **Zero theme = zero cascade lines.** Only structural plumbing remains.
**Only emit what the theme defines.** No defaults copied to elements.
**Deltas only.** Elements don't repeat family values.
**One file, all modes.** Default on `:root`, others on `[data-mode]`.
**Readable in devtools.** Each rule shows what it does.
Which children: `[element^="surface--"]`, `[element^="list--"]`, `[element^="table--"]` and `[layout="stack"]`, direct children only. The edges follow `data-dir` on the parent (none is a column).

The parent part of the selector is `:where(parent)`, so a part's own rule in the theme beats the bleed; the soft padding rule (`padding-<side>: var(--parent-pad-x|y)`) weighs the child alone, so a padding the theme writes on the part wins.

A Stack passes through: `[layout="stack"] > child { --parent-*: inherit }`, so the parts it holds bleed into the container's padding. A container inside a part publishes its own values, so the bleed stops there.
Inner radius = parent radius - parent border width, never below zero. The part never reaches over the border; the interior edges are straight. No modes.

A content is two boxes: `formatRule` sends every padding declared on `[element="surface--content"]` to `> [data-part="inner"]`, and the soft bleed padding does the same, so the outer box stays a bare scroll window.

reference.statement: Resolved in the DOM, never at build time. Every themed element publishes its padding, radius, border width and gap to its direct children as `--parent-*` variables (a companion rule `S > [element], S > [layout], S > [data-part]`, reset on every element so nothing inherits further). The bleed is fixed CSS reading them, emitted once per container whose `childrenSmartBleed` is true:

snippets.code:
shared/libs/ui/web/theme-engine/
├── conventions.ts     Family prefixes, element→family mapping, selector generation
├── emit.ts            Token-to-CSS emitters (boundary, interior, typography, etc.)
├── theme-process.ts   Main engine: walks theme, generates complete CSS output
├── build.ts           Build script: imports theme, runs engine, writes CSS file
├── index.ts           Barrel export
├── fonts/             Font files (owned by the lib)
├── generated/         Output CSS (one file per theme)
└── sandbox/           Visual test page

claims.text: The only structural knowledge is in `conventions.ts`:
**FAMILY_PREFIXES** — 9 entries mapping family keys to CSS prefixes
**ELEMENT_FAMILIES** — maps each element key to its family
**FAMILY_DEFAULTS** — sensible defaults per family (cursor, transition)
Add an element to the theme → the engine processes it automatically. No registry to update.

reference.statement: The engine has no hardcoded element lists. It walks the theme object dynamically and processes whatever it finds.

claims.text: These exist because tint, smart-bw, and alpha mixing require cross-property composition that plain CSS properties can't express.
**Everything else is plain CSS.** Padding, border-width, radius, shadow, cursor, transition, typography — set directly on cascade selectors. No indirection, no variable chains.

reference.statement: The engine uses **5 CSS custom properties** for composition: `--bg`, `--fg`, `--tint`, `--border-color`, `--bg-alpha`.

claims.text: **@font-face** — font file declarations
**Tailwind variant declarations** — `@custom-variant dark`
**L1: Primitives** — `:root` custom properties (colors, typography, spacing, etc.)
**L1b: Modes + Derivations** — per color scheme (`:root` default, `[data-mode]` others)
**Tailwind token registrations** — `@theme inline` block
**Base layer** — `@layer base` (body bg/fg, border defaults)
**Property application** — tint/alpha composition on `[element]` and `[layout]`
**Family & element extras** — scrim, placeholder, scrollbar, disabled, icons
**Cascade** — L2 families → L3 elements → L4 concepts → L5 contextual → axes → sizes

reference.statement: The generated CSS file reads as a coherent document:

claims.text: The app wears exactly one theme@version, chosen in `configs/theme/index.ts` (`APP_THEME = { theme, version }`); its vite config aliases `@theme` to that version's generated CSS:
Watch mode: `pnpm theme:watch` — rebuilds on theme or engine file changes.

reference.statement: Reads every `themes/<theme>/v<n>/theme.ts`, runs the engine, writes `themes/<theme>/v<n>/generated/<theme>.css` (+ `<theme>-fonts.css`) beside it.

reference.topic: Smart Bleed (the DOM, not the build)
reference.statement: The engine never resolves a parent's geometry at build time: it cannot know the parent of a node. The parent publishes, the child reads. The one remaining build-time resolution, the icon zones of a control, moves to the same variables.

reference.topic: What the Engine Does NOT Do

claims.text: No runtime JavaScript in the browser
No Shadow DOM isolation
No PR layout class generation
No runtime linting
No component modifications
